Definition: Costs incurred in the normla course of a business to generate revenues

Definition: Operating expenses are the usual and customary costs that a company incurs to support its main business activites
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Income Statement

Definition: Money made or lost outside of normal firm operations
Example: Gain on sale of operating equipment and losses on sale of land
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Income Statement

Definition:
An overall measure of the perfomance of a company. Net Income does not necessarily correspond to a net cash flow. A firm could have “good
income” but “poor cash flow” or vice versa (i.e., there are two dimensions to consider)
Example: Most agree that this is the most important accounting number.
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Income Statement

Definition: Relate to the company's financing and investing activites
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Income Statement

Definition: Net Income = Revenues - Expenses + Gains - Losses
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements>Income Statement

Definition: Demonstrates firms use of funds and where the funds came from AT A SINGLE POINT IN TIME. Formatted as assets in order of liquidity then liabilities in order of maturity, then shareholders' equity which has no required order
Example: Useful for evaluating capital structure and assessing risk and future cash flows
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements

Definition: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet

Definition: Reforms data purely on a cash basis, categorized into operating, investing, and financing activities
Example: One of the 5 required financial statements
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements

Definition: Economic resources that are owned or controlled by a company that have future economic benefit
Example: Only includes items that can be reliably measured, so assets like a a strong management team, well designed supply chain, or superior technology may not be reflected. But valid examples are Cash, Accounts Receivables (A/R), Inventory, Land, Buildings, Equipment, Copyrights, and Investments.
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet

Definition: Long-term assets cannot be easily converted to cash within a year
Example: Copy rights, equity investments, PPE
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet  > Assets

Definition: Current assets comprise assets that can be converted to cash within a year
Example: Accounts Receivables (A/R)
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet  > Assets

Definition: Current liabilities have maturities less than one year
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet  > Liabilities

Definition: Long-term liabilities have maturity longer than one year
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet  > Liabilities

Definition: Represents money a business owes to a financial institution; the specific document detailing the future obligations to repay those funds when a business borrows money
Example: Liability
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet  > Liabilities

Definition: Represents money owed to a company's employees.
Example: When employees have completed work for the business, but the company has not yet paid them for the value of that work
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet  > Liabilities

Definition: Category within the owners' equity section of the balance sheet. Represents the capital or resources that owners have contributed directly to the firm.
Example: Usually cash, but can take form of other assets like a building
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet > Owner's Equity (Shareholders' equity)

Definition: Another owners' equity account that functions simialrly to capital or common stack. Represents a different version or class of contributions made by owners to the business
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet > Owner's Equity (Shareholders' equity)

Definition: Beginning retained earnings + net income (mius loss) - dividends = ending retained earnings
Example: Critical to owners' equity account; accumulation of all past earnings since the company was created, minus all the dividends ever paid out to owners
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet > Owner's Equity (Shareholders' equity)

Definition: Distribution of funds paid by a business back to its owners or shareholders; extracts from retained earnings as a dividend, reducing retained earnings balance
Example: Information about dividends are found on 2 statements: The statement of shareholders' equity (as a deduction, visually explaining how the company's retrained earnings decreased during the period) or statement of cash flows as actual cash paid out to owners within the financing activties (because paying owners is considered a financing transaction)
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet

Definition: Money that is owed to a business by its customers, which helps assess and predict future cash flows. When a business determines that a business is not going to pay their account receivable, the company records that loss as a bad debt expense on their Income Statement
Example: Generally a business expects to convert receivables within 30 to 45 days, depending on the specific terms of the relationship with the customer
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet  > Assets

Definition: Future obligations to pay cash, transfer assets or provide services to another party.
Example: Examples of liabilities include account payable (A/P), notes payable (N/P), and wages payable (W/P)
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet

Definition:
The ownership interest in the net assets of an entity. 
Earnings (RE)
Example: Examples of owners’ equity include: Capital Stock, Preferred Stock, and Retained Earnings (RE)
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet

Definition: Debts that must be paid are listed first, while debts that do not need to be paid for a long time are listed last
Example: A bill due next week would be listed first, whereas a 25 year loan would be listed last
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet > Liabilities

Definition: Money that a business owes to a supplier or a provider of a service
Example: For example, if a retail company buys inventory from a supplier and the supplier gives them 30 days to pay the bill, the company will record that owed amount as an account payable during that 30-day window before the cash is actually transferred
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Balance Sheet > Liabilities

Definition: Reconciliation of the beginning and ending balances of shareholders' equity account (start balance, additions, reductions, and end balance)
Example: Main equity categories: Capital Stock, Retained Earnings, Treasury Stock, Other Comprehensive Income
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements

Definition: Mathematical process explaing how an account moved from its beginning balance at THE START OF A PERIOD to its ending blanace at the CLOSE OF THAT PERIOD
Example:
1. Identify balance of the account, carried over from the previous period's balance sheet
2. Identify specfic additions or reductions to the account during THE CURRENT PERIOD
3. Calculate final balance
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Statement of Shareholders' Equity

Definition: Financial statement that describes the entity's clash inflows and cash outflows during a period
Example: Only required since 1983
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements

Definition: Cash and cash equivalents: bank account balances, cash, coin, and short-term liquid investments
Example: Attributes tracked in the statement of cash flows
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Statement of Cash Flows

Definition: Cash transactions that enter into the determination of net income
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Statement of Cash Flows

Definition: Cash flows assoicated with items (like revenues and expenses) that were used to calculate or determine the net income on the Income statement
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Statement of Cash Flows > Operating Activities

Definition: Calculate net income purely from actual cash that came in and went out for specific operating categories DURING THE PERIOD
Example: Net income with only 'collections from customers' or 'payment for inventory'
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Statement of Cash Flows > Operating Activities

Definition: Start with net income taken from income statement, then make adjustments to get rid of non-cash items to convert the net income into a pure cash-from-operations format
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Statement of Cash Flows > Operating Activities

Definition: Cash transactions involved in the purchase and sale of PPE, other long-term assets and making/collecting loans (an investment to our firm)
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Statement of Cash Flows

Definition: Common category used to describe the long-term, tangible assets that a company purchases to operate its business
Example: Land, buildings, and equipment
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Statement of Cash Flows > Investing Activities

Definition: Cash transactions whereby resources are obtained or repaid to owners and creditors
Example: Note payable. Liability when firm borrows money
Branch: Financial Accounting > Financial statements > Statement of Cash Flows
